cases.architecture: Hapi 21 clinical records API where every route file is a plugin using Joi validation and route prerequisites, data access goes through a node-postgres pool in lib/db.js, and the session comes from an @hapi/cookie 'session' strategy exposing request.auth.credentials.
cases.why: The loadNote prerequisite selects the appointment note by request.params.noteId alone and the handler returns it, so any authenticated session -- including a patient-portal login -- can read another patient's SOAP note, name and MRN by changing the id in the URL; nothing compares note.patient_id with the session's own patient id or with care_team_member.

cases.architecture: Hapi 21 clinical records API where every route file is a plugin using Joi validation and route prerequisites, data access goes through a node-postgres pool in lib/db.js, and the session comes from an @hapi/cookie 'session' strategy exposing request.auth.credentials.
cases.why: The prerequisite's WHERE clause is the guard: alongside the id it binds the session's own patient id and an EXISTS over care_team_member for the session's clinician id, so a summary the caller has no relationship to never leaves Postgres and the handler answers 404.

cases.architecture: Hapi 21 clinical records API where every route file is a plugin using Joi validation and route prerequisites, data access goes through a node-postgres pool in lib/db.js, and the session comes from an @hapi/cookie 'session' strategy exposing request.auth.credentials.
cases.why: request.query.panel is spliced into the WHERE predicate as a single-quoted literal and request.query.sort is spliced into the ORDER BY clause, and the assembled string is then executed by query(sql, values); either query parameter can therefore close the literal or append clauses and rewrite the statement against the whole lab_result table.

cases.why: Same filter-and-sort listing, but the panel filter is pushed onto values and referenced as $n, and the sort key is translated through the SORT_COLUMNS allowlist (which Joi.valid also enforces), so no caller-supplied text ever becomes part of the SQL string.

cases.architecture: Hapi 21 clinical records API where every route file is a plugin using Joi validation and route prerequisites, data access goes through a node-postgres pool in lib/db.js, and the session comes from an @hapi/cookie 'session' strategy exposing request.auth.credentials.
cases.why: request.query.file is joined straight onto LETTER_ROOT with path.join and the result is opened with createReadStream and streamed to the caller; Joi only caps its length, so a value containing ../ segments escapes the letter store and returns any file the API process can read.

cases.architecture: Hapi 21 clinical records API where every route file is a plugin using Joi validation and route prerequisites, data access goes through a node-postgres pool in lib/db.js, and the session comes from an @hapi/cookie 'session' strategy exposing request.auth.credentials.
cases.why: Same enclosure stream, but two guards stand in front of createReadStream: Joi restricts file to the ENCLOSURE_NAME pattern (32 hex characters followed by .pdf, which admits no separators and no dot-dot segment), and the path resolved from the store root must still start with that root or the request is rejected.

cases.architecture: Hapi 21 clinical records API where every route file is a plugin using Joi validation and route prerequisites, data access goes through a node-postgres pool in lib/db.js, and the session comes from an @hapi/cookie 'session' strategy exposing request.auth.credentials.
cases.why: The only check on this bulk export reads claimedRole from request.payload.actingRole, falling back to the x-clinic-role header, and both are attacker-controlled; any authenticated session can send actingRole: 'pharmacist' and export active prescriptions with names, MRNs and dates of birth for up to 200 arbitrary patient ids.

cases.architecture: Hapi 21 clinical records API where every route file is a plugin using Joi validation and route prerequisites, data access goes through a node-postgres pool in lib/db.js, and the session comes from an @hapi/cookie 'session' strategy exposing request.auth.credentials.
cases.why: The same bulk export, but authorization comes from the session: the route declares auth: { strategy: 'session', scope: ['pharmacist', 'prescriber'] } so Hapi rejects other callers before the handler, and the handler re-checks me.roles from the credentials while treating the payload's actingRole as a display hint only.

cases.architecture: Hapi 21 clinical records API where every route file is a plugin using Joi validation and route prerequisites, data access goes through a node-postgres pool in lib/db.js, and the session comes from an @hapi/cookie 'session' strategy exposing request.auth.credentials.
cases.why: The route turns authentication off (auth: false) and decides access from the first entry of the x-forwarded-for header, which any client can set; an unauthenticated caller who sends X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.5 receives the whole access log, including actor emails, patient names and MRNs.

cases.why: The same access-log query and response, but the guard is the cookie strategy's scope check -- auth: { strategy: 'session', scope: ['compliance'] } -- evaluated against the server-side session row, and no request header takes part in the decision.

cases.architecture: Hapi 21 clinical records API where every route file is a plugin using Joi validation and route prerequisites, data access goes through a node-postgres pool in lib/db.js, and the session comes from an @hapi/cookie 'session' strategy exposing request.auth.credentials.
cases.why: The handler selects sl.expires_at with the share row but never compares it with the current time -- only revoked_at is checked -- so a share token keeps releasing the lab result, patient name and date of birth long after the link was meant to lapse, and the comment's claim that a nightly sweep removes expired rows is not a guard the request path enforces.

cases.architecture: Hapi 21 clinical records API where every route file is a plugin using Joi validation and route prerequisites, data access goes through a node-postgres pool in lib/db.js, and the session comes from an @hapi/cookie 'session' strategy exposing request.auth.credentials.
cases.why: The same public share-token flow, but alongside the revocation check the handler compares the link's lifetime against the clock: new Date(link.expires_at).getTime() must be finite and still in the future or the request is refused, so a lapsed (or unparseable) expiry releases nothing even when the nightly cleanup has not run.
